verdict.rationale: Microsoft's own Outlook REST getting-started docs point users to Graph Explorer to run sample REST calls. The API reference pages (e.g. sendMail) exist alongside it. That counts as first-party runnable examples, but the evidence is a single mention, with no detail on how interactive it is or how it ties into the reference pages. The probes found no OpenAPI spec at the guessed paths, which doesn't contradict the claim. missing for 10: documentation of Graph Explorer's interactive features (auth, editable requests, live responses), runnable examples embedded in the API reference pages, a machine-readable spec, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples
